what_changed: A bug in `scripts/orchestrator_runner.py` caused `state.current_run.partial_reasons` (and `partial: true`) to carry forward from prior orchestrator invocations into subsequent runs. The state-initialization block was reordered so every new run unconditionally begins with a fresh `current_run` — `partial: false` and `partial_reasons: []` — before checking whether the prior run was stale. The stale-clear diagnostic (`stale_current_run_cleared`) is preserved by writing into the newly-initialised `current_run` via `add_partial`. The old `carried_partial` / `carried_reasons` reads were deleted. Three subprocess-driven integration tests (`tests/orchestrator/test_state_carry_forward.py`) lock the no-carry-forward contract, and `CHANGELOG.md` was updated with a v0.1.3 entry.
why: Transient failure reasons — such as `schema_invalid: source-collector: 'prs' is a required property` and `push_failed` — from a prior orchestrator run would reappear in the next run's state even when that run was otherwise clean. The bug was observed during Mode B testing against ADIS (linked to CCE-9) where the same `schema_invalid` reason accumulated across consecutive nightly runs. Root cause: the state-init block read `current_run.partial` and `current_run.partial_reasons` from the existing state dict and copied them into the new `current_run`, so any reason ever recorded would persist until `verify_runner` promoted the run to `last_successful_run`. The fix inverts the default — start clean, let persistent conditions re-accumulate naturally from the current run's own dispatches.
notes: No Jira context was supplied despite CCE-5 and CCE-9 being linked; the PR body, plan file, and roadmap spec provided complete context. The spec file (`2026-05-20-cce5-9-batch-prep-roadmap-design.md`) predates this PR (committed at c474d98) but appears in files-changed — it was updated to reflect resolved acceptance criteria. CHANGELOG.md already shows a v0.1.4 entry above v0.1.3, confirming CCE-9 has since shipped on top of this change.
